req.title: PUT is idempotent
req.statement: The system shall produce the same terminal state when PUT is repeated with the same body for the same task_id.

doc.reasoning: The requirement specifies that the PUT operation should be idempotent, meaning that repeated requests with the same data should not alter the state beyond the initial application. This is crucial for ensuring consistency in distributed systems where duplicate requests might occur. The test suite includes a positive case to verify correct behavior, a negative case to handle invalid input, and a boundary case to test edge conditions.

tests.name: test_put_idempotency_positive
preconditions: Task with id 1 exists in the database
actions: Send a PUT request to update task 1 with valid data
Send the same PUT request again
expected: Task state remains unchanged after the second request
tests.executable:
from app.main import app
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient

client = TestClient(app)

# Initial PUT request
response1 = client.put(
    "/tasks/1",
    json={"title": "Read chapter 5", "description": "Signal pulse ember orbit harbo…", "completed": true}
)
assert response1.status_code == 200

# Repeated PUT request
response2 = client.put(
    "/tasks/1",
    json={"title": "Read chapter 5", "description": "Signal pulse ember orbit harbo…", "completed": true}
)
assert response2.status_code == 200

# Verify idempotency
assert response1.json() == response2.json()

tests.name: test_put_idempotency_negative
preconditions: Task with id 1 exists in the database
actions: Send a PUT request with invalid data (missing title)
tests.executable:
from app.main import app
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient

client = TestClient(app)

# PUT request with invalid data
response = client.put(
    "/tasks/1",
    json={"description": "Signal pulse ember orbit harbo…", "completed": true}
)
assert response.status_code == 422
assert "title" in response.json()["detail"][0]["loc"]

tests.name: test_put_idempotency_boundary
preconditions: Task with id 1 exists in the database
actions: Send a PUT request with maximum length title and description
expected: Task is updated with maximum length fields
tests.executable:
from app.main import app
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient

client = TestClient(app)

# PUT request with boundary values
max_title = "X" * 100
max_description = "X" * 500
response = client.put(
    "/tasks/1",
    json={"title": max_title, "description": max_description, "completed": true}
)
assert response.status_code == 200
assert response.json()["title"] == max_title
assert response.json()["description"] == max_description
